newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shipping firm to pay Japan for oil spill.
newsitem.headline: Russia shipping firm to pay Japan for oil spill.

text.p: The owner of a Russian tanker which sank and spilled thousands of tonnes of oil off the Japanese coast last week will reimburse Japan fully for the environmental disaster, Interfax news agency said on Friday.

The agency quoted Sergei Vitkazov, chief executive of Prisco Traffic Ltd, the owner of the vessel, as telling a news conference in Russia's Far Eastern city of Nakhodka that the company would use money from insurance for compensation.
Interfax quoted Vitkazov as saying the tanker and its cargo had been insured for up to $500 million.
The UK P&I Club, managed by Thomas Miller, said that it provides pollution liability insurance for the tanker, the Nakhodka, through a protection and indemnity policy.

P&I policies provide a maximum of $500 million cover for marine pollution incidents, the first $5.0 million being paid by the lead club, in this case the UK, a spokesman for the UK P&I Club told Reuters.
The next $25 million is covered by the P&I group, which represents most P&I clubs. Claims above $30 million are covered by reinsurance.
Vitkazov also said his firm was ready to help Japan with the clean-up by providing special freight ships and that the insurer had already contracted an unnamed British company to take part.
Japan has not yet estimated the value of losses.

Authorities there still do not know the full extent of the accident, one of the worst oil spills in Japanese history. They initially estimated that 3,700 tonnes (26,000 barrels) of fuel oil leaked from the tanker but on Tuesday said this figure appeared too low.
The Japanese Fisheries Agency said coastal shellfish-gathering operations sustained damage and it feared the oil would harm offshore net and bottom fishing for shrimp and crabs.
The 13,157-tonne Nakhodka was carrying a total of 19,000 tonnes (133,000 barrels) of fuel oil.
The Nakhodka was built 26 years ago and Japanese authorities said the age of the ship, which was heading to Russia from China, was probably a factor in its break-up in the rough seas.
